name: MAX1044ESA+T
title: MAX1044 / ICL7660: CMOS switched-capacitor voltage converters, 1.5V to 10V
summary: The MAX1044 and ICL7660 are CMOS charge pumps that turn a positive supply of 1.5V to 10V into its negative; in other connections they double it (with two diodes), halve it, or give a negative multiple of it. The basic inverter needs only two outside capacitors; four power MOSFET switches and the oscillator are on chip, and no output diode is needed. The output is not regulated: it falls with load through the output resistance (65Ω typ for the MAX1044 at 5V), and 10mA comes with a 0.5V drop. On the MAX1044, tying BOOST to V+ speeds the oscillator up about six times; both are pin compatible with the ICL7660 and LTC1044.

circuits.title: Test circuit for the electrical characteristics
circuits.description: The circuit the electrical table is measured in: a 10µF pump capacitor across CAP+ and CAP-, a 10µF reservoir from VOUT to ground, a 0.1µF bypass on V+ and a load resistor RL from V+ to VOUT. Switches set the test state: one joins BOOST to V+, one connects OSC either to an external clock or to a timing capacitor COSC, and one grounds LV.

parts.note: OSC to the external clock or to COSC

circuits.title: Basic negative voltage converter
circuits.description: The plain inverter: the pump capacitor C1 sits across CAP+ and CAP-, the reservoir C2 holds the output with its positive side on ground, and a bypass capacitor sits on V+. The output settles near the negative of the supply. BOOST and OSC are left unconnected so the internal oscillator runs at its nominal rate.
notes: LV to ground is required for V+ below 3.5V.

circuits.title: Negative voltage converter with COSC and BOOST
circuits.description: The inverter with its oscillator adjusted: BOOST is wired to V+ to raise the rate about six times, and a capacitor COSC from OSC to ground lowers it. LV is left open.

circuits.title: External clocking
circuits.description: The inverter run from an outside clock: a CMOS or TTL gate, its two inputs tied together to take the clock, drives OSC. A 10kΩ resistor from V+ to OSC pulls the clock up to the supply; it is required with a TTL gate.

circuits.title: Negative voltage converter with BOOST and LV connections
circuits.description: The common inverter with a 0.1µF bypass on V+ and LV grounded. BOOST may be joined to V+ to run the oscillator faster.
notes: The BOOST to V+ link is optional; without it BOOST is left open.
A bypass capacitor of 0.1µF to 10µF on V+ is recommended.

circuits.title: Voltage doubler
circuits.description: A positive doubler driven from CAP+: one diode from V+ feeds the top of the pump capacitor C1, whose other side is on CAP+, and a second diode passes that charge to the reservoir C2. VOUT pin is grounded. The output is twice V+ less two diode drops; Schottky diodes reduce the drops.

circuits.title: Voltage divider
circuits.description: Splits the supply in half: the part runs from V+ with its VOUT pin grounded, and its GND pin is the half-supply output, held by C2 to ground. C1 is the pump capacitor across CAP+ and CAP-. LV may be tied to the half-supply node.
notes: The LV link to the half-supply node is optional.
A third capacitor may be added between V+ and the output.

circuits.title: Combined positive and negative converter
circuits.description: One part gives both a negative rail and a doubled positive rail. C1 and C3 are pump and reservoir for the inverted output; C2 and C4 are pump and reservoir for the doubled output. C2 runs from CAP+ to a node fed from V+ through one diode, and a second diode passes that charge to C4. Both outputs have higher output impedance because they share one charge-pump driver.

circuits.title: Cascading devices for a larger negative output
circuits.description: Three inverters stacked to give about -3 times V+. Each later stage is powered between the two rails before it: the second takes ground as its V+ and the first output as its GND, the third takes the first output as its V+ and the second output as its GND. Each stage has its own 10µF pump capacitor and 10µF reservoir to ground. Output resistance grows quickly with each stage.
notes: n is the number of devices in the chain.

circuits.title: Paralleling devices to reduce output resistance
circuits.description: Two or more inverters in parallel, each with its own pump capacitor C1, all driving one shared reservoir C2. Output resistance falls as one over the number of devices and the current available rises.

parts.note: pump capacitor of U2 (C1 of the second device)

notes: Device n repeats the second device; LV is shown optionally grounded on each.

circuits.title: Shutdown by a gate and diode on OSC
circuits.description: A logic gate stops the oscillator through a 1N4148 diode into OSC, with a 10kΩ pull-up from V+ on the gate side (needed for TTL). The gate's inputs are tied together as the shutdown control. Of the three shutdown methods this one loads OSC least, and turning the diode round sets whether a high or a low level shuts the converter down.

operation.text: A charge pump with four internal MOSFET switches. In one half cycle S1 and S3 close and the pump capacitor C1 charges to V+. In the other half S2 and S4 close, which puts C1's positive side on ground and its negative side on VOUT, so C1 sits in parallel with the reservoir C2 and tops it up. Over many cycles C2 approaches -(V+); switch resistance and load current keep the real output a little short of that.

Besides the switches the part holds their drive circuits, an oscillator followed by a divide-by-two stage, and an internal regulator that the LV pin can bypass. A 1MΩ resistor inside joins BOOST to V+.

Most uses need only the pump and reservoir capacitors, and their type is not critical. A bypass capacitor of 0.1µF to 10µF on V+ is recommended. Larger, low-ESR capacitors reduce both ripple and output impedance and so raise efficiency. Smaller values will do at smaller output currents.

LV bypasses the internal regulator, which improves low-voltage behaviour and allows operation down to 1.5V. For compatibility with the ICL7660 and LTC1044, ground LV below 3.5V and leave it open above 3.5V. On the MAX1044, LV may be grounded at any supply: this improves low-voltage performance and raises the oscillator frequency, at the cost of more quiescent current and lower efficiency at high supply voltages. On the Maxim ICL7660 LV must be open above 5V. At low supplies with LV open, keep the LV, BOOST and OSC connections short or shielded so that interference does not jitter the oscillator.

Normally BOOST and OSC are left open and the internal oscillator runs at its nominal rate. A higher frequency lowers audio interference, output resistance, ripple and the capacitor sizes needed; a lower frequency lowers quiescent current and raises efficiency. The frequency is not precise: only a minimum of 1kHz and 5kHz for the MAX1044 and a typical 10kHz for the ICL7660 are given. Where an exact frequency is needed, drive OSC from an outside oscillator.

On the MAX1044, joining BOOST to V+ raises the oscillator frequency about six times. That lowers output impedance and ripple, allows smaller capacitors and moves switching noise above the audio band. With OSC driven from outside BOOST has no effect and is left open; it is also left open in normal use.

A capacitor from OSC to ground slows the oscillator. That improves efficiency at light load because quiescent current falls, but raises ripple and output impedance; bigger C1 and C2 make up for it. Keep the OSC trace short so stray capacitance does not pull the frequency down. For example, an inverter pumping at 4kHz to 5kHz with 10µF capacitors draws about 70µA quiescent while giving 20mA. 100pF on OSC sets the oscillator to 400Hz and the quiescent current to about 15µA; holding 20mA then needs 100µF capacitors. 1000pF on OSC sets 40Hz, the highest efficiency possible: with 100µF capacitors the output reaches 2mA, no-load quiescent current is 10µA and power conversion efficiency 98%.

OSC can be driven by an outside clock up to 400kHz, to synchronise the converter or to push it higher out of the audio band. The pump and ripple frequencies are half the clock frequency. A faster clock allows smaller capacitors and raises quiescent current. OSC switches at V+ - 2.5V for V+ ≥ 5V, and at V+ / 2 below 5V. A clock that does not swing up to V+ needs a 10kΩ pull-up.

The output is not regulated; it falls with load by the output resistance, which depends mostly on oscillator frequency and capacitor size, and so also on temperature and supply voltage. With 5V in and 10µF capacitors the output resistance is typically 50Ω: about -5V at light load and about -4.5V at 10mA. Analog loads should be checked for their supply rejection, since ripple and drop grow at heavy load. Output impedance comes down by paralleling parts, using bigger C1 and C2, or tying the MAX1044's BOOST to V+.

C1 and C2 must charge at start-up, so the part draws an inrush current, and in operation it takes short current bursts from the supply. A high-impedance supply can sag too far during these bursts for the part to work. High supply or ground impedance, or long traces and large loops to the pump capacitors, create switching noise and EMI. Remedies: feed the part from a low-impedance source; put a low-ESR bypass capacitor close to the IC from V+ to ground; keep the traces to the pump capacitors short; keep the ground pins of the capacitors and the IC close together; and leave copper around the converter as power and ground planes, which a two-sided board makes easy.
Schottky diodes reduce the diode drops VD. For true doubling or more output current the MAX660 is suggested.

Three or more devices can be chained, but output impedance climbs steeply: two cascaded MAX1044s have about five times the output resistance of one. An inductive switching regulator (MAX755, MAX759, MAX764 or MAX774) may serve better.

Three ways to shut the converter down all act on OSC, and the extra capacitance they put on OSC lowers the oscillator frequency. (a) A CMOS or TTL gate drives OSC through a 1N4148 diode with a 10kΩ pull-up to V+ for TTL; it loads OSC least, and the diode's direction picks a high or low shutdown level. (b) An open-drain 74HC03 or open-collector 74LS03 NAND gate, powered from V+ and ground, with its inputs tied together, pulls OSC directly. (c) A 74HC126 or 74LS126 three-state buffer, powered from V+ and ground, drives OSC, controlled by its output-enable input.

Taking any input above V+ or below ground can latch the part up, so outside signal sources must not be applied before the part is powered. Never exceed the maximum supply rating. Fit C1 and C2 the right way round. Do not hold V+ shorted to ground for long while other pins see more than 5.5V. VOUT (pin 5) must not rise above GND (pin 3); a diode across C2, anode at VOUT and cathode at LV, prevents it.
